I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation. That is the system I trust most because it fits my weather, my irrigation conditions, and the way I need to manage labor. I want steady grain, not a risky switch. I will put all my main land into winter wheat first and then follow it with summer maize on the same fields. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care more about stable yield and easier field management than saving a little seed cost. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate level, not too light and not too heavy, because I want the crop to stand well and fill grain without wasting money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in my area depends more on timely water, especially around jointing and grain filling. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage before wheat because it helps me make a cleaner seedbed, and I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest because that saves time and lets me plant fast. I will spray only when needed for the common weeds, insects, and diseases I usually see, and I will keep the plan simple enough that I can manage it steadily through the whole season.
